chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abī ʿUbaydah al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a menstruating woman who hears the verse of sajdah. He said: If it is from the obligatory prostration verses, she prostrates when she hears it.

So this report does not contradict the first report, because it does not state that it is permissible for her to recite the verses of obligatory prostration. It only says: when she hears the verses of obligatory prostration, she prostrates. This also is to be understood as recommendation, because she is in a state in which prostration is not permissible for her.

key_terms.السَّجْدَةَ: the prostration verse or act of prostration
key_terms.الْعَزَائِمِ: the Qur'anic verses of obligatory prostration

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a menstruating woman hears a verse of obligatory sajdah?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of a menstruating woman hearing a verse requiring sajdah. It distinguishes between hearing and reciting the verses of obligatory prostration, and the compiler explains that the instruction to prostrate is understood as recommendation in light of her state.
